author: Jimmy LaRoue
title: Amid violence and violations, Chances use permit revoked - NewsBreak
text:
By Jimmy LaRoue ,
1 hours ago
HAMPTON, Va. (WAVY) — Hampton City Council unanimously voted Wednesday to revoke the use permit to Chances Restaurant and Lounge amid multiple violations and violence there, including a homicide in May.
Man dies following shooting at Chances Restaurant and Lounge in Hampton The city’s Planning Commission had recently voted to recommend that council revoke the use permit for the restaurant on Settlers Landing Road following several violent incidents. Among the grounds for revoking the use permit:
Pattern of violent incidents and ineffectiveness of permitholder’s responses indicates security staffing is not “sufficient to monitor and control patron behavior” Continued violence indicates that permitholder does not fully “report all criminal activity” or “cooperate” with HPD investigations Multiple VABC violations document that permitholder does not “comply with all restrictions or requirements imposed by VABC” Oct. 1 revocation of VABC license indicates permitholder’s failure to “obtain and maintain all applicable licenses to conduct the business” The city’s May 15 Notice of Violation regarding indoor smoking indicates permitholder’s violation of state law The city’s May 6 Notice of Violation regarding window treatments indicates permitholder’s violation regarding window transparency The permitholder’s entity status with the State Corporation Commission is “Pending Inactive,” which if not corrected will cause its legal existence to lapse Hampton Planning Commission recommends City Council to revoke use permit for local lounge Hampton Police and city officials have cited a lack of security and crowd management, among other issues the restaurant has been dealing with.
During the commission meeting, a Hampton Police officer had noted the public concern over fights and firearm-related offenses at the restaurant, laying out several violent incidents outside Chances and playing a video of the moments gunshots rang out in front of it during a recent shooting.
A use permit for Chances had been approved in March 2024, allowing for live entertainment and alcohol sales, and it opened for business that October.
A presentation to council outlined security incidents, including an April weapon law violation, an individual with a gun in May, followed by a homicide four days after that, and then multiple incidents in September, including:
Sept. 6 : Fight involving 15-20 patrons that took place at Chances Sept. 13 : Another fight involving numerous Chances patrons that took place there Sept. 20 : At least 15 firearm rounds were shot by at least two different shooters at the location, and a patron was observed breaking a storefront window Hampton Police analysis noted crowd management concerns and a lack of security oversight for loitering, and public concern due to fights and firearms-related offenses.
Virginia ABC suspended Chances’ alcohol license May 8 due to its failure to “take reasonable measures to prevent an act of violence,” referencing the May 5 homicide.
However, that license was reinstated May 21, subject to added security conditions. Again, though, Virginia ABC suspended Chances’ license Oct. 1 for violating the May 21 security conditions, citing three incidents in the span of two weeks in September.
The business, which has had 25 calls for service this year — three of those calls were for fights — also received two notices of violations in May, one for applying a window treatment that impeded visibility into the restaurant, and another for allowing customers to smoke indoors in violation of the Virginia Indoor Clean Air Act.
No one spoke during a scheduled public hearing on the matter ahead of council’s vote.
